title: How a researcher uses Codex and ChatGPT to search for new antimicrobial molecules
contentSnippet: César de la Fuente’s lab uses Codex and ChatGPT to search living and extinct genomes for antimicrobial candidates to fight drug-resistant infections.

title: Now everyone can put data to work
contentSnippet: Meet the Data agent in ChatGPT Work. Connect company data, uncover insights, and build interactive dashboards with AI using natural language.

title: 1.1.1.1 now supports post-quantum DNSSEC, all 2,420 bytes of it
contentSnippet: 1.1.1.1 now validates DNSSEC signatures using NIST’s post-quantum ML-DSA-44 algorithm. Here is how we manage 2,420-byte signatures and downgrade risks at scale.

title: Expanding AI access and cyber defense for federal, state, local, and tribal governments
contentSnippet: OpenAI and GSA will offer eligible federal, state, local, and tribal governments $0 license fees, 50% off usage, and expanded cyber defense support.

title: GitHub availability report: August 2026
contentSnippet:
In August, we experienced five incidents that resulted in degraded performance across GitHub services.

title: Build more natural voice experiences with GPT‑Live‑1 in the API
contentSnippet: GPT‑Live‑1 brings natural, full-duplex voice conversations to the API, with stronger instruction following, custom voices, and telephony support.

title: Introducing Amazon EBS Volume Clones across AWS accounts
contentSnippet: AWS introduces Amazon EBS Volume Clones with cross-account copy, so you can create copies of your EBS volumes into other AWS accounts and optionally re-encrypt them with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key in the target account.

title: Threat Matrix: Mapping threats across cloud web applications
contentSnippet:
Microsoft introduces the Cloud Web Applications Threat Matrix, a MITRE ATT&CK-aligned framework that helps defenders understand, prioritize, and mitigate threats to cloud-hosted web apps and serverless platforms.
The post Threat Matrix: Mapping threats across cloud web applications appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

title: Passkey-themed social engineering leads to identity and cloud compromise
contentSnippet:
Passkey-themed social engineering is being used to compromise identities and enable broader cloud attacks. Learn how threat actors establish MFA persistence, abuse Microsoft Graph for reconnaissance, and access SharePoint, OneDrive, and email data, along with key detection and mitigation guidance.
The post Passkey-themed social engineering leads to identity and cloud compromise appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.
